newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Debt vol poised, awaiting EU announcement.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Debt vol poised, awaiting EU announcement.

text.p: Implied volatility of debt options on LIFFE and MATIF was slightly higher on Monday, amid expectations of a positive outcome to the Amsterdam European Union (EU) summit, options brokers said.
"Everything is on hold, volatility is staying firm," said Luke White, options broker at Fimat Futures in London.

In Bund options, the July at-the-money straddle exercisable into the September future traded earlier at 5.53 percent, brokers Tullett & Tokyo said. August Bund options volatility was slightly above Friday's levels at 5.30-5.38 percent, and September was also up at 5.27-5.34 percent.
The underlying September Bund future was at 101.80, up 23 basis points on the day at 1105 GMT.
In BTPs, September options volatility was higher too, at 7.87 percent. December was quoted at 7.80-8.02 percent.
A senior French official said on Monday he expected the EU summit to reach agreement by early afternoon in Europe on a jobs and growth resolution and a budget stability pact.
"A lot of people are sitting these rising markets out until we get some more news out there," said one broker from a U.S. firm.
BTP futures recorded an all-time contract high of 132.39 earlier, while the notionnel future is aiming for its all-time high of 132.94.
At 1105 GMT, September BTP futures were at 132.24, up 45 basis points on the day, and September notionnel futures were at 129.32, up 40 basis points.
Options volatility will sell off on an EU agreement, but will rocket if no agreement emerges, brokers said.
"All bets will be off, and there will be a squeeze in volatility," said White.

"If you look at the open interest, people are still long of Italian and Spanish bond futures, despite recommendations to get out of them. If there is no agreement, they will go into U.S. Treasuries and gilts," he added.
Activity was brisk in Bund options, brokers said, with volatility firmer in out-of-the-money puts. One European firm sold 500 July calls at the at-the-money 101.50 strike, they said.
In BTPs, another firm sold 500 September puts at the 129.50 strike, brokers added.
